name: Disorder of Lipid Metabolism

criteria.description: Persistent elevation of serum cholesterol and/or triglycerides above age- and sex-specific reference ranges
Presence of xanthomas, lipemia retinalis, or hepatosplenomegaly
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in lipid metabolism (e.g., LDLR, APOB, PCSK9)
Family history of premature cardiovascular disease or lipid metabolism disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent elevation of serum lipids plus either clinical features or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of biochemical, clinical, and genetic data.

pathognomonic.notes: Firm nodular lesions over tendons, especially Achilles and extensor tendons
Lipid deposition in the peripheral cornea

common.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to lipid accumulation
Milky appearance of retinal vessels due to high triglycerides

occasional.notes: Inflammation of the pancreas secondary to hypertriglyceridemia
Nerve damage possibly related to lipid storage
Chest pain due to coronary artery disease

searchTerms: fatigue due to poor heart function

rare.notes: Muscle weakness due to lipid accumulation
Rare neurodegenerative disorder with lipid storage

rare.symptomName: Aortic valve stenosis due to lipid infiltration
searchTerms: narrowing of aortic valve from fat buildup
aortic valve blockage due to lipids
heart valve stiffening from fat deposits

laboratory: Reduced HDL cholesterol in some cases
imaging: Corneal arcus visible on slit-lamp examination
genetic: Pathogenic variants in LDLR, APOB, PCSK9, LIPA, or other lipid metabolism genes
other: Histopathology of xanthomas showing lipid-laden macrophages

redFlags: Sudden onset pancreatitis in young patient
Rapidly progressive xanthomas or neurological symptoms
references: Goldstein JL, Brown MS. Familial hypercholesterolemia. In: The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. 2001.
National Lipid Association. Clinical Guidance on Lipid Disorders. 2023.
